name: Avoid Macros with High Fan-In (z/OS Assembler)
description:
Avoid Macros with High Fan-In (Fan-In > X). The Fan-In of an Artifact is the number of other Artifacts that are referencing it. When computing the Fan-In of an Artifact, multiple accesses to it from the same Artifact are counted as one access.
The threshold level is a parameter that can be changed at will.
For a z/OS Assembler Macro, these Artifacts are the z/OS Assembler Programs that invoke it. Another Macro invoking it does not count. A Macro is often shared on purpose by many Programs: the default threshold is higher than for Programs.
output:
Associated to each z/OS Assembler Macro with violations, the Quality Rule provides:
- The Fan-In
rationale:
An Artifact referenced by many other Artifacts is costly to change: a change can impact all of them, and all of them have to be tested again.
Changeability and testability decline with increasing Fan-In.
remediation: Check that the Macro is shared on purpose. Otherwise split it into smaller Macros, so that each Program invokes only what it uses.
alternativeName: Avoid Macros with High Fan-In (z/OS Assembler)
